approval.cost: Partner Center account fee not stated in the docs read; Microsoft 365 Certification stated as carrying no monetary cost (developer blog)
approval.trigger: Three distribution tiers, three approvers. Sideloading: no review at all, gated only by the tenant's 'Upload custom apps' setting. Publish to your org: your own Teams admin approves in the admin center (your IT admin, not Microsoft). Teams Store: Microsoft approval is required, via Partner Center, validated against the Teams Store validation guidelines and Commercial Marketplace certification policies with deep functional tests across desktop, web, and mobile. Publisher verification must be completed BEFORE you submit.
approval.wait: Store: detailed test report aimed within 24 working hours of submission (stated); total approval time not stated (resubmission rounds vary); after approval, allow at least one business day for the app to appear in the Store (stated)

blockers.detail: The manifest carries two IDs that do different jobs: bots[].botId points at the Azure Bot registration, while webApplicationInfo.id points at the Entra app registration used for SSO/Graph. They may legitimately differ. Worse, if your bot uses a User-Assigned Managed Identity, no app registration is created automatically; you must create one separately and reference it.
blockers.howToClear: Map both IDs deliberately during setup and verify which one each config surface is asking for.
blockers.title: The two-ID trap (botId vs webApplicationInfo.id)

blockers.detail: Customer tenant admins control custom-app upload, org app settings, app permission policies, and Entra admin consent. An admin can block third-party apps or your specific app entirely, even after Microsoft approves it for the Store. This gate repeats per customer, forever.
blockers.howToClear: Build an admin-facing onboarding path (consent + app approval instructions) as part of your product, like every Microsoft-ecosystem integration.
blockers.title: Tenant admins can block you after Microsoft approves you

blockers.detail: Silent SSO depends on setup details that are easy to miss: requestedAccessTokenVersion must be set to 2 by hand in the Entra manifest, the access_as_user scope must be exposed, and the Microsoft 365 client apps (Teams, Outlook, Edge, etc.) must be pre-authorized. Miss these, or lack IT admin consent, and users get consent prompts on first use per platform instead of silent sign-in.
blockers.howToClear: Follow the SSO registration checklist exactly and get admin consent pre-granted in customer tenants where possible.
blockers.title: SSO is only silent if you pre-authorize everything

alternatives: Bot Framework OAuth connections (OAuth card sign-in against Entra or a third-party IdP like Google/GitHub, when the agent must sign the user into an external service)
Sideload-only custom app (no Store ambitions; still needs per-tenant admin settings to allow upload)
flavor.recommended: A Teams app (bot and/or message extension) backed by a multitenant Microsoft Entra app registration with SSO enabled and delegated Microsoft Graph permissions
flavor.why: There is no Teams-specific OAuth provider: authentication is Entra ID. With SSO, the Teams client sends a token to your service and the Bot Framework Token Service exchanges it for a Graph token with your defined permissions, so users already signed into Teams authenticate silently after one-time consent. Teams distribution and identity are separate layers; plan for both.

humanMust: Supply the Azure/Entra tenant and create the registrations (Agents Toolkit automates the mechanics)
Complete publisher verification (an organizational identity check) before Store submission
Create the Partner Center account and sign listing agreements for the Store
Each customer's tenant admin: enable custom-app upload, approve the app, and grant consent
name: Microsoft Teams
nuances: Secret values are shown only once at creation; copy immediately.
Application ID URI formats are strict (api://botid-{id} for a standalone bot; lowercase domain required; mixed-case domains unsupported on Android).
Store rules with teeth: apps 'mustn't display advertising, including dynamic ads, banner ads, and ads in message' (a Must-fix item).
Sideloading is unavailable in GCC High, DoD, and 21Vianet tenants; org publishing in GCC needs the government channel option for bots/message extensions.

The compliance ladder is optional beyond the Store: Tier 2 Publisher Attestation is a self-assessment ('most attestations can be completed in one hour or less'); Tier 3 Microsoft 365 Certification is a full analyst assessment with penetration testing and yearly renewal.
From July 2026, new Store submissions for channel-enabled apps must use manifest schema 1.25 or later (stated in the publish docs).
prerequisites: An Azure/Entra tenant and an app registration
An Azure Bot resource (for bot/message-extension capabilities)
A client secret (or managed identity setup) and your Application ID URI
For the Store: a Partner Center developer account and completed publisher verification

steps.detail: In your bot's Entra app registration: set requestedAccessTokenVersion to 2 in the manifest; Expose an API with the Application ID URI (api://botid-{YourBotId} for a standalone bot); add the access_as_user scope with consent text; pre-authorize the Microsoft 365 client applications (Teams mobile/desktop/web, Microsoft 365 app, Outlook, Edge) so users aren't prompted; create a client secret (visible only once); configure the redirect URL platform; add the delegated Graph permissions you need.
steps.title: Configure the Entra app for SSO

steps.detail: Set the messaging endpoint URL, then Add OAuth Connection Settings: name, Entra as provider, client ID, client secret, Token Exchange URL = your Application ID URI, tenant ID, scopes. A Test connection check is provided.
steps.title: Configure the Azure Bot OAuth connection

steps.detail: Manifest declares webApplicationInfo (Entra app ID + resource URI) and botId; zip it with the icons; validate with the Developer Portal's App validation tool (supported only for apps with bot capability).
steps.title: Build and validate the Teams app package

steps.detail: Upload/sideload the package in Teams to test. Requires 'Upload custom apps' enabled in the Teams admin center (Setup policies), which can take up to 24 hours to become active (stated).
steps.time: Minutes to upload; setting up to 24 hrs
steps.title: Sideload and test

steps.detail: Org: submit to your Teams admin center; the app sits as Submitted/Blocked in Pending approval until an admin publishes it, then app permission policies control who sees it. Store: submit via Partner Center; fix Must-fix/Blocker items from the validation report (aimed within 24 working hours) over as many rounds as needed; after approval allow at least one business day for Store availability.
steps.time: Org approval is your admin's pace; Store timeline varies by resubmission rounds
steps.title: Distribute: org publish or Teams Store

tagline: Two layered objects, not one: a Teams app package for distribution, and an Entra app registration for identity. SSO can be silent, but only if you pre-authorize everything; and every customer tenant's admin remains a permanent gate.

time.active: ~1-2 hrs of SSO/bot configuration plus package work; your own service code on top
time.total: Same day to sideloaded testing; Store approval takes as many validation rounds as your app needs
time.waiting: Custom-app upload setting up to 24 hrs; Store test report aimed at 24 working hours per round
